newsitem.title: USA: Calif exports surge 13.5 pct in first half of 1996.
newsitem.headline: Calif exports surge 13.5 pct in first half of 1996.

text.p: California exports surged by 13.5 percent to $51.9 billion in the first half of 1996, Gov. Pete Wilson said on Thursday.
The growth was fueled by renewed and diversified sales to Mexico and Japan, Wilson said in a statement. He said the growth supported about 117,800 jobs.
Exports to Mexico, California's fourth-largest market, increased by $700 million in the first half of 1996, or 21.4 percent, compared to a $300 million decline for all of 1995.
"California exports to Mexico have grown in reflection of an improving Mexican economy," Wilson said.
Exports to Japan surged 29.4 percent to $9.87 billion in the first half of 1996.

Exports to Canada, California's second-largest market, increased 21 percent. Sales of industrial machinery and computer equipment along with electronics and electrical equipment represented 72 percent of export growth with Canada.

South Korea continued to be California's third-largest export market. Exports grew at a more moderate pace of 18.8 percent in the first half of 1996 following a phenomenal rise of 41 percent during 1995.

"California is fast emerging as the world leader in high technology development," Wilson said. "Our dominance in computer equipment, electronics and industrial machinery continues to fuel our explosive gain in exports."
"California is back and is in full swing," Wilson said.
